data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A small research team should adopt an existing experiment tracker only if their workflow is strictly observational; however, if the research involves active learning loops where the tracker must function as a real-time controller modifying experimental parameters, they must build a custom minimal tracker to avoid the 'integration tax' and causal fragility inherent in wrapping mismatched tools.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The team lacks the engineering bandwidth to maintain even a minimal custom state machine.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The active learning component is low-frequency or batch-based rather than real-time.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"An existing tool offers a native plugin architecture that exposes full control without significant integration tax.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The decision hinges on the 'Control Theory Boundary': existing tools are optimized for passive data logging (observation), creating high friction when forced into active control roles. Custom builds are justified solely by the need for a tight feedback loop where the state machine of the tracker is identical to the causal model of the experiment, eliminating the latency and schema-mismatch risks of adapter layers.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
